# Refactor guard: downtime-worker split invariants

**Parent:** WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 — decompose `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`
**Type:** task (test-first gate — created and landed BEFORE any code moves)

## Goal

As a reviewer/auditor of the `downtime-worker.ts` split, I want one automated
gate that fails whenever the split breaks a behaviour-preserving invariant, so
that every extraction child can land safely without touching any existing test
file and without a reviewer having to re-derive the invariants by hand.

## Context

Parent AC2/AC3/AC4/AC5 require: an unchanged public surface at
`./downtime-worker.js`, unmodified test files, no new circular imports, and a
single `dispatchInFlightCount` declaration. Nothing in the repo enforces these
today (there is no `madge`/`dependency-cruiser`; `vitest` is the only test
runner), so this child builds the enforcement first.

Current facts captured at plan time (2026-10-23, `dev` @ 9,362 lines):

- 36 consumer files (`src/**/*.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/*.ts`) import **134
  distinct symbols** from `./downtime-worker.js`.
- `let dispatchInFlightCount = 0` is declared once (currently line 3141) and is
  mutated only inside `dispatchDowntimeWork` (lines 5772/5790/6259).
- Pre-existing cycle: `stalled-work.ts` imports values from
  `./downtime-worker.js` while `downtime-worker.ts` imports **types only** from
  `./stalled-work.js` — the one cycle the split must not widen into a runtime
  cycle.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. New **additive** test file `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.split-guard.test.ts`
   (vitest) exists and passes on the current tree before any production code moves.
2. Committed baseline `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.split-baseline.json`
   records the 134 consumer-imported symbol names plus provenance (generation
   command, source commit, timestamp).
3. Public-surface gate: the test asserts every baseline symbol is still exported
   by `./downtime-worker.js` (value or type), so a lost re-export fails the suite.
4. Single-flight gate: exactly one production `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker*.ts`
   file (excluding `*.test.ts`/`*.fixtures.ts`) declares `dispatchInFlightCount`.
5. Barrel/cycle gate: no production `downtime-worker.*.ts` module contains a
   runtime (value) import of `./downtime-worker.js`, and the static import graph
   of `downtime-worker*.ts` modules contains no cycle outside the recorded
   baseline allowlist (`stalled-work ↔ downtime-worker`, type-only).
6. Size gate: every production `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker*.ts` module is
   ≤1,000 lines, excluding an exported `SPLIT_ALLOWLIST` that initially contains
   only `'downtime-worker.ts'`; a further assertion proves the allowlist only ever
   shrinks (it must remain a subset of the plan-time list).
7. Each gate is proven to fail on a deliberately broken input (a synthetic
   >1,000-line module, a dropped export, a runtime barrel import, a duplicated
   counter) — the failure modes are unit-tested, not assumed.
8. No existing test file is modified; the change is additive only.
9. `/skill:test` (changed scope) passes, including the new guard suite.
10. A comment on this item records the baseline generation command and the
    gate-to-parent-AC mapping.

## Minimal implementation

1. Generate the baseline: scan `src/**/*.ts` + `packages/herdr/src/*.ts` for
   `import ... from '.../downtime-worker.js'`, normalise `type ` prefixes,
   dedupe, sort → JSON with provenance fields.
2. Write the guard test with four checks (exports, single-flight, cycle/barrel,
   size+allowlist), each as a separately named `it()` so failures are legible.
3. Add the negative-case fixtures (temp files under `os.tmpdir()` or inline
   strings parsed by the same helpers) and assert each check reports a failure.
4. Export `SPLIT_ALLOWLIST` from the test file's helper section so the final
   child (barrel finalisation) can empty it in one line.
5. Run `/skill:test` (changed scope); record the guard output in a comment.

**Key Files:**

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.split-guard.test.ts` — new
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.split-baseline.json` — new
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — read-only (no edits in this child)

## Dependencies

None — first child; every extraction child is blocked by this one.

## Notes

- Adding a test file is additive and does not violate parent AC3 ("no test file
  is modified"); the parent brief's Risks section explicitly calls for "a
  targeted test assertion" to enforce AC5.
- Test-writing guidance: `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md`.

# Finalise downtime-worker barrel and docs

**Parent:** WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 — decompose `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`
**Scope:** the residual `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` content (module doc comment + import/export wiring) plus the documentation updates and the final verification pass for the epic.

## Goal

As a consumer of the downtime worker, I want `downtime-worker.ts` to be a thin,
honest barrel that re-exports exactly the symbols other modules actually use, and
I want the dispatcher docs to show the module layout, so that the public surface
is discoverable and the epic's acceptance criteria are verifiable in one pass.

## Scope

- Reduce `downtime-worker.ts` to: module-level doc comment (kept provenance,
  trimmed to a short overview + pointer to the module layout), and
  `export … from './downtime-worker.*.js'` statements only.
- Re-export **only symbols actually imported by consumers** (134 baseline symbols
  captured by the split-guard child); stop re-exporting symbols no consumer and
  no sibling module uses.
- Empty `SPLIT_ALLOWLIST` in `downtime-worker.split-guard.test.ts` so the size
  gate now covers every `downtime-worker*.ts` module including the barrel.
- Documentation: add a "Module layout" section to
  `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (module → single responsibility → key
  exports), update `packages/herdr/README.md` if it names internals, and fix any
  code comments that still describe the monolith.
- Record the final verification evidence on the epic.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `wc -l packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` ≤ 250, and the file contains no
   function/type/const declarations — only the doc comment and re-exports.
2. The barrel re-exports exactly the 134 consumer-imported symbols from the
   baseline, and no symbol that neither a consumer nor a sibling module imports;
   a scan comparing barrel exports against the baseline (plus sibling-module
   imports) is recorded as evidence.
3. `SPLIT_ALLOWLIST` is empty and the split-guard test proves every
   `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker*.ts` production module (including the
   barrel) is ≤1,000 lines; the allowlist-shrink assertion is satisfied.
4. The split-guard public-surface, single-flight, cycle and size gates all pass;
   the import graph has no cycle beyond the recorded pre-existing type-only
   `stalled-work ↔ downtime-worker` cycle, and no split module imports the
   barrel at runtime.
5. The 15 `downtime-worker.*` test suites plus the whole `packages/herdr` suite
   pass **unmodified**, and the full repo suite passes (`/skill:test` full).
6. `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` contains a "Module layout" section listing
   every module created by the split with its single responsibility, and no doc
   or comment still refers to `downtime-worker.ts` as a 9,000-line monolith; a
   search of the repository docs, `docs/` site sources and the project wiki
   confirms no other page documents the old internal layout (result recorded in
   the evidence comment).
7. The build is green (`npm run build` / `npm run build:shared` as applicable)
   and `tsc` reports no new errors.
8. A comment on this item records: `wc -l` output for every module, the guard
   test output, the suite result, and the symbol → module mapping — enough to
   audit epic AC1–AC8 without re-running anything.
9. Every epic AC (1–8) is verified with the evidence above; any AC that cannot
   be met is raised as an OPEN QUESTION on the epic instead of being silently
   waived.

## Minimal implementation

1. Delete the remaining moved code from `downtime-worker.ts`; build the barrel
   export list from the baseline JSON (and sibling-module imports) so it is
   exactly the used surface.
2. Empty `SPLIT_ALLOWLIST`; run the guard suite and inspect each gate's output.
3. Rewrite the module doc comment: short overview, the ranking contract
   (Herdr list head is the sole ranking path), fail-closed note, and a pointer to
   the module layout table in the docs.
4. Add the docs module-layout section; update `packages/herdr/README.md` if it
   references internals.
5. Run `/skill:test` (full) + build; record the evidence comment; verify AC1–AC8.
6. Verify moved blocks match the pre-split source (`git show <pre-split>:...`
   diff review) and note the result.

**Key Files:**

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — becomes the thin barrel
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.split-guard.test.ts` — allowlist emptied
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — module layout section
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — internal references, if any
- all `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.*.ts` — read-only verification

## Dependencies

Blocked by: orchestrator child. Final child of the epic.

## Notes

This child is the only one permitted to change the barrel's exported symbol set
(Q2 refinement). Removing an unused re-export is intended — but a symbol that a
test file imports is *used* and must stay, because test files may not be
modified (parent AC3).

# Reservation handshake fixtures and contract tests (test-first slice)

## Summary

Pin the local-proxy reservation handshake as exported TypeScript types,
fixtures and contract tests **before** any client code exists, so the reserve
client (C2) and the one-per-idle-window guard (C3) are built against pinned,
tolerant-parsing behaviour and a red-then-green test contract.

## Covers parent ACs

- Parent **AC1** (reserve client) — the granted/refused shapes and their
  parsing are pinned here; the client itself lands in C2.
- Parent **AC2** (failure-mode backcompat) — the absent/500/timeout fixtures
  that C2's fail-open path is tested against are defined here.

## Target outcome

`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.fixtures.ts` and a new
`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.reserve.test.ts` describe the reservation
contract from the parent description:

- `POST {proxyUrl}/llama/local/reserve` request: the pane's expected token
  size, priority and cache state.
- Granted response: gate ticket id + TTL, surfaced as
  `X-Local-Reservation` on the pane's first request.
- Refused response: HTTP 429 with `{ reason, retry_after_s }`
  (reasons such as `reserved-fallback`, `prefill-gate`, `queue-full`).
- Endpoint absent (404) / server error (500) / hang → fail-open `null`
  (today's polling behaviour), never a throw.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **C1-AC1 — types and constants.** Exported reservation types
   (`LocalReservationRequest`, granted/refused result shapes) and header-name
   constants (`X-Local-Reservation`, plus the `X-Local-Preference` /
   `X-Local-Route` / `X-Local-Fallback-Reason` names used by C4) live in
   `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` (or a small dedicated module
   re-exported from it) and are importable by tests.
- **C1-AC2 — fixtures.** `downtime-worker.fixtures.ts` gains
   `reserveGranted`, `reserveRefused429`, `reserveEndpointAbsent`,
   `reserveServerError` and `reserveTimeout` built in the established
   `prefillPacingStatus()` style (typed, commented, no ad-hoc inline objects
   in tests).
- **C1-AC3 — contract tests (red first).** `downtime-worker.reserve.test.ts`
   asserts: granted body → typed ticket with a finite TTL; 429 body → typed
   refusal with `reason` and `retry_after_s`; non-JSON/garbage body,
   missing ticket, negative/non-finite `retry_after_s` → fail-open `null`;
   404/500/timeout → fail-open `null` with no throw. Tests are written before
   the parser and fail against the current tree.
- **C1-AC4 — traceability.** Each test name cites the parent AC it serves
   (`AC1` / `AC2`) so the C3 and C5 reviews can trace coverage.
- **C1-AC5 — no behaviour change.** No production dispatch behaviour changes
   in this slice (`downtime-worker.*` tests other than the new file stay
   green); the parser is exported but not yet called on the dispatch path.

## Dependencies

- **None** (blocking parent only). This is the test-first slice that C2/C3 build on.

## Constraints

- The proxy item (llm-manager `LP-0MVIKPCSG002B0NL`) is **not yet implemented
  or present in the llm-manager worklog** (verified 2026-10-23: no
  `llama/local/reserve` handler in `proxy/`). Pin the contract exactly as
  documented in the parent description; keep parsing strict-but-tolerant so
  additive proxy fields cannot break us.
- Reuse the existing fixture/parse patterns (schema-v2 `LlamaStatus`,
  `parseOptionalCount`, fail-closed `null` semantics).
- No new polling loop; the reserve client introduced in C2 piggybacks the
  single-flight status poll.

## Risky assumptions

- Ticket TTL and the exact granted-body field names are unknown until the
  proxy lands — mitigation: tolerant parsing + a single typed accessor, so a
  rename is a one-line change.
- The refusal reasons enumerated in the parent (`reserved-fallback`,
  `prefill-gate`, `queue-full`) may not be exhaustive — mitigation: accept
  any non-empty string reason, never branch on an unknown one.

**Key Files:**

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — reservation types, header
  constants, tolerant parser.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.fixtures.ts` — reservation fixtures.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.reserve.test.ts` — new contract tests.

## Deliverables

- Reservation types, header constants and parser (exported, unused on the
  dispatch path).
- Fixtures for granted / refused / absent / 500 / timeout.
- Contract tests, red before the parser and green after it.

# Reserve client with fail-open dispatch gate

## Summary

At each dispatch decision the worker calls `POST {proxyUrl}/llama/local/reserve`
on the existing single-flight poll cadence: a granted ticket releases the
pane spawn (ticket forwarded to the pane so its first request carries
`X-Local-Reservation`); a 429 refusal defers with `retry_after_s` and records
the refusal; an absent/500/timeout endpoint degrades to exactly today's
polling behaviour. The decision log gains the reservation evidence.

## Covers parent ACs

- Parent **AC1** (reserve client) — implementation of the reserve call, the
  granted→launch / refused→defer paths.
- Parent **AC2** (failure-mode backcompat) — absent/500/timeout → today's
  polling behaviour, covered by tests.
- Parent **AC4** (decision-log evidence, dispatch half) — ticket state,
  `admit`, `projected_wait_s`, `retry_after_s` recorded per decision.

## Target outcome

The dispatcher never launches without a ticket: it asks, gets a ticket, then
launches — never poll-then-hope.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **C2-AC1 — reserve client (parent AC1).** when the proxy serves the reserve endpoint (fixture), a dispatch first receives a ticket and only then launches with the reservation header; a refused ticket defers with `retry_after` and is recorded (`downtime-worker.mock.test.ts`-style mocked fetch, following the existing fixture pattern).
   Concretely: the spawned pane receives the granted ticket (env
   `PI_LOCAL_RESERVATION_TICKET`, forwarded by `send-to-pi.sh` /
   `run-pi-agent.sh`) so its first request carries `X-Local-Reservation`.
- **C2-AC2 — refusal recorded.** The proxy's refusal reason
   (`reserved-fallback` / `prefill-gate` / `queue-full`) is carried into the
   decision entry with `retry_after_s` and a distinct header token via
   `decisionHeaderToken`, and the spawn path never runs.
- **C2-AC3 — failure mode backcompat (parent AC2).** endpoint absent/500/timeout → exactly today's polling behaviour, no crash, no stuck pane (tests for each): one test per failure mode (404 / 500 / timeout), each asserting dispatch proceeds as if the reserve endpoint did not exist, with no retry storm.
- **C2-AC4 — decision-log evidence (parent AC4, dispatch half).** Every
   polled decision entry records `reservationTicket` (id, granted at),
   `admit` (true/false), `projectedWaitS` and `retryAfterS` via the extended
   `DecisionEntryFields`.
- **C2-AC5 — no new polling (parent constraint).** The reserve call rides the
   existing single-flight poll cadence — a test asserts at most one reserve
   request per poll and no standalone timer/poll loop.
- **C2-AC6 — pacing preserved (parent constraint).** Pacing only reduces
   concurrency: the reserve call never raises the free-slot budget and never
   bypasses the fail-closed `slots-unavailable` / `capacity-saturated` /
   prefill gates (regression tests stay green).

## Dependencies

- **Blocked by:** C1 (reservation fixtures + contract tests).
- **Blocks:** C3 (race guard) and C5 (docs/suite gate).

## Constraints

- Reservation piggybacks the status-poll cadence (no new polling loop).
- Fail-open: an older proxy (no reserve endpoint) is fully supported.
- Surgical: extends `WL-0MVHSZRZQ00482QX`'s pacing with the atomic claim;
  does not rewrite the dispatcher.
- Ticket TTL bound: a granted ticket that cannot be forwarded to the pane
  (spawn failure) must be treated as released/expired, never leaked.

## Risky assumptions

- The exact ticket field names/TTL come from the C1 pinned contract; a rename
  in the proxy lands as a one-line accessor change.
- Reservation latency per dispatch is acceptable (parent calls it out) — the
  C2-AC5 test asserts call-count bounds so latency cannot silently grow.

**Key Files:**

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `fetchLocalReservation`,
  dispatch-gate wiring, decision-log fields.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.fixtures.ts` / `.reserve.test.ts` /
  `.test.ts` — reserve + backcompat + call-count tests.
- `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh`, `shared/run-pi-agent.sh` — ticket
  env passthrough to the pane.
- `packages/herdr/README.md`, `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — reservation
  handshake + ticket forwarding documented (parent AC5 partial).

## Deliverables

- `fetchLocalReservation` client + dispatch-gate integration (granted/refused/
  fail-open), runner ticket passthrough, decision-log evidence fields,
  tests, doc sections.

# One-per-idle-window reservation race guard

## Summary

Assert and enforce the operator requirement that an idle window produces
**at most one** launch: after a ticket-backed launch no further pane starts
until a fresh status tick shows `local_prefills_in_flight <
local_max_concurrent_prefills` **and** a new reservation is granted for that
specific launch. Pin the same-tick two-instance race with a test.

## Covers parent ACs

- Parent **AC3** (one-per-idle-window) — the whole slice.

## Target outcome

Two herdr instances observing the same idle window cannot both launch; the
loser defers with the proxy's own refusal evidence instead of queueing a
doomed pane that later falls back to remote.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **C3-AC1 — one-per-idle-window (parent AC3).** two instances observing the same idle window produce at most one launch; the second defers with the refusal evidence (test modelling the same-tick race).
   The test runs two `createDowntimeWorker` instances against one mock proxy in
   the same tick and asserts exactly one pane is spawned, the second dispatch
   refused by the reservation call.
- **C3-AC2 — post-launch suppression (parent AC3).** After a successful
   launch, no second pane launches on later ticks while
   `local_prefills_in_flight >= local_max_concurrent_prefills`; only a fresh
   status tick with headroom **and** a ticket granted for that specific launch
   permits another spawn.
- **C3-AC3 — losing-instance evidence (parent AC4, dispatch evidence).** The
   losing instance's decision entry records the refusal reason,
   `retry_after_s` and `admit: false`, with a header token distinguishable
   from `prefill-cap`/`prefill-gate` so an operator can tell a lost race from
   a paced stop.
- **C3-AC4 — coordination-path parity.** The same one-per-idle-window rule
   holds on the coordination-leader dispatch path
   (`dispatchFromCoordination`) — no second launch in the same idle window
   there either (test).
- **C3-AC5 — no regression.** The guard never admits a dispatch the per-slot /
   saturated / prefill gates would refuse and never changes single-instance
   behaviour when the proxy grants normally (existing `downtime-worker.*`
   suites stay green).
- **C3-AC6 — docs (parent AC5 partial).** `packages/herdr/README.md` and
   `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` document the one-per-idle-window rule
   and how it composes with the existing coordination leader.

## Dependencies

- **Blocked by:** C2 (reserve client + dispatch gate).
- **Blocks:** C5 (docs/suite gate).

## Constraints

- The proxy is the arbiter (atomic reservation grant); herdr does **not** add
  a second distributed lock — it only refuses to launch without its own
  granted ticket.
- Never raise the concurrency budget; never bypass the fail-closed per-slot
  handling (`WL-0MUXVPXAZ005RESW`).
- Reuse the C2 reserve client; no duplicate reservation code path.

## Risky assumptions

# Per-turn local preference and route logging

## Summary

Give agent panes a per-turn capacity claim: a pi extension injects
`X-Local-Preference` (`local-only` for work the operator marks local-first,
`remote-ok` for background work) on the Local Proxy provider path and records
`X-Local-Route` / `X-Local-Fallback-Reason` response headers into a route log,
so a refusal is immediate and honest instead of a silent 120 s proxy-side
wait. The herdr runner sets the preference per spawn from a policy knob.

## Covers parent ACs

- Parent **AC4** (per-turn preference) — the whole slice (the dispatch-side
  decision evidence is delivered by C2-AC4).

## Target outcome

An agent turn either gets a local route or receives an immediate, recorded
fallback decision; the operator can read per-session route evidence next to
the dispatch decision log.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **C4-AC1 — per-turn preference (parent AC4).** the runner sends `X-Local-Preference` per configured policy, parses `X-Local-Route`/`X-Local-Fallback-Reason`, and records both in the decision log (tests).
   Concretely: the herdr agent runner (`packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh` /
   `run-pi-agent.sh`) sets the preference for each spawn from a policy knob
   (proposed `HERDR_LOCAL_PREFERENCE` env / herdr setting
   `downtimeLocalPreference`, default `local-only` for downtime panes and
   `remote-ok` for background/scheduled work); the extension sends that value
   on every proxied request and writes one JSONL route line per turn to the
   bounded route log; pure-module and runner-script tests assert both values
   and the unset (no header) case.
- **C4-AC2 — route log detail.** Each route line carries session id,
   timestamp, route, fallback reason and model, appended to a bounded log
   (proposed `.worklog/local-route.log`, rolling convention like
   `downtime-dispatches.log`, capped at 2000 entries). Absent or malformed
   headers write no entry and never throw.
- **C4-AC3 — fail-open backcompat.** With no knob set, no headers from an
   older proxy, or the extension absent, requests are byte-identical to
   today's (no header, no log, no behaviour change); a capture failure never
   breaks a turn (tests).
- **C4-AC4 — dispatch correlation.** Route-log entries carry the pi session
   id and the reservation ticket (when one was forwarded), so a dispatcher
   decision can be correlated with the turns it produced (test + doc).
- **C4-AC5 — docs (parent AC5 partial).** `packages/herdr/README.md` and
   `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` document the preference policy knob and
   the route log, with matching code comments.

## Dependencies

- **None** inside this item — independent of C1–C3 (separate pi extension +
  runner path) and can run in parallel; it only shares the contract header
  names pinned in C1.
- **Blocks:** C5 (docs/suite gate).

## Constraints

- The pi extension is the only place that can see the response headers (pi
  owns the request path); reuse the established extension pattern
  (`~/.pi/agent/extensions/proxy-sse-signals` wraps the Local Proxy provider's
  `streamSimple` with a capturing fetch) and the repo installer
  (`scripts/install-pi-extension.sh`).
- Fail-open only: a missing preference knob or a broken extension must never
  block or alter a turn.
- No new polling loop; route logging is per response.
- No secrets/PII in the route log.

## Risky assumptions

- Pi's provider override can inject a request header and read response
  headers (precedent: `proxy-sse-signals` reads the body stream via a
  capturing fetch; the same wrapper exposes `Response.headers`).
- The route log location is acceptable as a per-root `.worklog/` artifact
  (same convention as the existing downtime logs); confirm at implementation
  if the producer prefers `~/.pi/agent/logs/`.

**OPEN QUESTION (producer):** is `local-only` the right default for downtime
panes (fail fast to remote) vs a wait-for-local default? Default proposed from
the parent's "work the operator marks local-first" wording; the knob makes it
configurable either way.

**Key Files:**

- `packages/tui/extensions/local-preference/index.ts` (new provider wrapper)
  and `packages/tui/extensions/local-preference/local-preference.ts` (new pure
  module, unit-testable without pi) — precedent
  `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/`.
- `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh`, `shared/run-pi-agent.sh`,
  `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` (env/knob plumbing),
  `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` (knob default + clamp).
- `packages/herdr/README.md`, `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`.

## Deliverables

- Local-preference pi extension + tests, runner/knob plumbing, bounded route
  log writer, doc sections.

## Summary

Add a `wl doctor prefix` subcommand that changes the configured project prefix in `.worklog/config.yaml` and renumbers every existing work item to the new prefix, preserving each item's suffix (e.g. `OSL-0MVK31VYQ007CN37` → `CC-0MVK31VYQ007CN37`). The flow must ask for confirmation before it changes anything, default to a read-only preview, and emit a machine-readable rename map.

## Motivation

Requested from the ContentCreator project (`/home/rgardler/projects/ContentCreator`), whose configured prefix is `OSL` while the project is now branded `CC`. 1207 work items carry the `OSL-` prefix, and `wl doctor foreign-items` correctly classifies any item whose prefix differs from `.worklog/config.yaml` as foreign — so editing the prefix by hand would make the whole backlog look foreign and break cross-project lookups.

## Scope (proposed)

- `wl doctor prefix` — read-only preview: current prefix, counts of items/comments/dependency edges/audit records, and sample renames.
- `wl doctor prefix --to <PREFIX>` — declare the target prefix (validated: non-empty, no `-`, ASCII alphanumeric).
- `wl doctor prefix --to <PREFIX> --confirm` — apply: rewrite the config prefix, then rewrite every ID-bearing record (`workitems.id`, parent references, dependency edges, comments' `workItemId`, audit results, waivers, and any other ID column), and write a rename map (`osl→cc` pairs) to `.worklog/prefix-rename-<timestamp>.json`.
- Confirmation gate: interactive run without `--confirm` prompts and requires an explicit `y`; a non-TTY run without `--confirm` aborts with no writes and a non-zero exit.
- Idempotent: re-running after a successful rename reports a no-op.
- `--json` output for scripting.
- Docs: `DOCTOR_AND_MIGRATIONS.md` and `CLI.md`.

## Acceptance criteria (draft)

- [ ] `wl doctor prefix` (preview) reports counts and sample renames and changes nothing; covered by unit and temp-store integration tests.
- [ ] `--confirm` rewrites every ID-bearing record (items, parents, dependency edges, comments, audit results, waivers) and writes the rename map.
- [ ] Confirmation gate: non-interactive without `--confirm` aborts with a non-zero exit and zero writes; interactive requires explicit `y`.
- [ ] Re-running after a successful rename is a no-op, and a mid-run failure leaves the store recoverable (transactional or a documented rollback).
- [ ] `wl doctor foreign-items` reports zero foreign items after a confirmed rename.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated (CLI.md, DOCTOR_AND_MIGRATIONS.md, code comments).
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Out of scope

Rewriting ID references held outside the worklog store — code comments, docs, test fixtures, git commit messages, branch and worktree names. The requesting project owns that sweep and will use the rename map.

## Related

- Requested by work in the ContentCreator project (`discovered-from` recorded there).

## Summary

`.worklog/config.defaults.yaml` in this repo has no `syncAllowedAuthors` list, so `wl sync` runs the author-identity gate in strict mode: it refuses to merge any incoming commit on `refs/worklog/data` whose author email differs from the store's `git config user.email`. The shared ref carries 3,687 commits authored by `pi@local` while this checkout's `user.email` is `sorra@thewizardscode.com`, so agent-initiated `wl sync` runs here were refused and needed `--allow-foreign-author`.

## Fix (as shipped)

Declare a narrow allow-list in `.worklog/config.yaml` — **not** in `.worklog/config.defaults.yaml`: that file is this repository's project *template* (`projectName: TestProject`, `prefix: TEST`), so identities listed there would leak into every project created from it.

```yaml
syncAllowedAuthors:
  - 250240+SorraTheOrc@users.noreply.github.com
  - pi@local
```

Never use `null`/`true` (allow-all); empty-author commits must stay refused.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] The effective `syncAllowedAuthors` (defaults merged with `.worklog/config.yaml`) lists both identities, and `config.yaml` never shadows a defaults entry with a narrower list.
- [x] `wl sync` and `wl sync --dry-run` succeed in this checkout without `--allow-foreign-author`.
- [x] A guard test drives the real config merge and the real gate: listed authors accepted, unknown author refused, empty author refused even with the allow-all override (`tests/config-sync-allowed-authors.test.ts`).
- [x] Full project test suite passes with the new changes — re-verified at HEAD `d688a370` on 2026-10-27 (`run_tests.py --scope full`: 283 files / 4131 tests, 0 failures). The earlier blocker `tests/unit/persist-write-detection.test.ts` was fixed and closed via `WL-0MVM9E3SV003III0` (commit `40143a30`).

## Observed

Found while filing WL-0MVM8V79C003XH2J (prefix rename request) on 2026-10-24; the first sync was completed with `--allow-foreign-author` as a one-off, then `git pull` was run and `wl sync` re-tested.

## Notes (verification session 2026-10-27)

Implementation commit `6c598200` was already on `dev`; this session verified all ACs against HEAD `d688a370` and closed the lifecycle. Effort: Small; Risk: Low (effort-and-risk estimates persisted).

Producer finding from the machine-hygiene session (2025-10-21): propose_remediations() in skill/machine-hygiene/scripts/pressure_analysis.py emits a renice action for every large RSS contributor under memory/swap pressure without inspecting the target's current nice value. In the observed run every proposed target was already at nice 19 or 0, and the targets included two live test suites (AI_Hell vitest, tce-the-rising browser suite) - the action would have slowed active work.

Suggested fix (from producer): skip renice when min(nice) over the target pids is already >= the proposed nice value, and surface the current nice value in the action's reason/target so the operator can see why an action is proposed or suppressed.

Note: this is deliberately separate from the duplication fix in WL-0MVI8YJ1H007HUEZ (dedupe + single render); this item is the semantic safety change and needs process-nice collection support.

Scope: scanning niceness (/proc/<pid>/stat field 19) for target pids, suppressing no-op renicces, and tests for both suppressed and emitted cases. Related: skill/machine-hygiene/scripts/pressure_analysis.py (propose_remediations), metrics collection if nice must be collected centrally.

# Default downtime local preference should be remote-ok

**Headline:** Flip the downtime locality default from `local-only` to `remote-ok`
so unattended downtime work never queues the local slot the operator may need,
while `local-only` remains an explicit per-deployment opt-in.

## Problem statement

Downtime-dispatched panes default to `local-only`, so on a contended local slot
the proxy refuses the request immediately instead of falling back: the
unattended work simply does not run, even though remote capacity is available.
`local-only` is only *safe* when the operator has deliberately said "this work
must run here" — as a blanket default it strands work that could have run
remotely, and (see WL-0MVNUJG04005QL7G) cannot serve prompts above the local
provider's context ceiling at all.

## Users

- **Producer/operator running downtime dispatch.** Wants backlog work to keep
  moving unattended without competing for the local slot they need for
  interactive work.
- **Operator of a deliberately local-first deployment.** Wants the current
  fail-fast-local behaviour preserved, selected explicitly rather than by
  default.
- **Operator auditing dispatch behaviour.** Wants the route log to show
  `preference: remote-ok` on a default deployment, so "which default applied?"
  is evidence, not guesswork.

User stories:

- As a producer, I want downtime-dispatched panes to default to `remote-ok` so a
  contended local slot does not silently stall my backlog.
- As a producer running a local-first box, I want `downtimeLocalPreference:
  local-only` to keep today's behaviour exactly, with no other switch needed.
- As an operator, I want the route log of an unconfigured deployment to record
  `remote-ok`, so I can confirm the new default is live after deployment.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Default constant.** `DOWNTIME_LOCAL_PREFERENCE` is `'remote-ok'` in
  `packages/herdr/src/local-preference.ts`; the module header documents
  `remote-ok` as the default and `local-only` as the per-deployment opt-in,
  cross-referencing this item and the superseded default in
  WL-0MVLJTV03000KIQZ.
- [ ] **Clamp.** `clampDowntimeLocalPreference` resolves every absent/invalid
  input (`undefined`, `null`, `''`, `'auto'`, `'both'`, `'Local-Only'`,
  `' remote-ok'`, `42`) to `remote-ok` via the constant, still passes
  `local-only` / `remote-ok` through verbatim, and never invents a value.
- [ ] **Settings default.** `defaultSettings.downtimeLocalPreference` is
  `'remote-ok'`, and `loadSettings` resolves a missing file, a file without the
  key, and an out-of-alphabet persisted value to `remote-ok`;
  `tests/herdr/settings.test.ts` (default + clamp cases) and
  `packages/herdr/src/local-preference.test.ts` are updated to pin it.
- [ ] **Dispatch paths inherit the default.** With no `downtimeLocalPreference`
  in `settings.json`, downtime backlog dispatch, own-backlog fallback,
  audit-batch continuation and scheduled-prompt dispatch all forward
  `remote-ok` to the pane (`--local-preference remote-ok` and
  `HERDR_LOCAL_PREFERENCE=remote-ok`), asserted by regression tests; the
  Worklog pi extension route-log test records `preference: "remote-ok"` for a
  `remote-ok` pane so the observable route log matches.
- [ ] **`local-only` stays selectable.** With `downtimeLocalPreference:
  'local-only'` persisted, every dispatch path still forwards `local-only`
  (existing C4-AC1 forwarding tests stay green) and nothing overrides it.
- [ ] **Documentation.** `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`,
  `packages/herdr/README.md` (setting list + per-turn local preference section)
  and `packages/tui/extensions/README.md` (where its prose implies a default)
  state `remote-ok` as the default, `local-only` as the opt-in, and make the
  scheduled/background inheritance explicit; related code comments in
  `settings.ts`, `downtime-worker.ts` and `local-preference.ts` are updated.
- [ ] **Testing/validation gate.** Changed-scope tests pass before commit and
  the full project test suite passes via `/skill:test` (no ad-hoc test runs).

## Constraints

- **Wire contract unchanged.** The request header alphabet stays exactly
  `local-only | remote-ok`; no new header, value or proxy (LP) change is in
  scope.
- **Fail-open preserved.** Unset/empty/invalid input still resolves to the
  default (now `remote-ok`), never throws and never invents a preference.
- **Optional internal field semantics unchanged.** `DowntimeWorkerConfig.config()
  .localPreference` stays optional: absent still means "no `--local-preference`,
  no `HERDR_LOCAL_PREFERENCE`, no route-log line" (byte-identical launch for
  hand-built/legacy configs). The new default reaches production panes through
  `loadSettings()` → plugin `config()`, which always supplies a value.
- **`BACKGROUND_LOCAL_PREFERENCE` stays separate** (`remote-ok`) and remains the
  fallback for callers that supply no knob. Scheduled prompts continue to take
  the knob when present — so an explicit `local-only` deployment also makes
  scheduled work local-only. That inheritance must be documented, not silently
  changed.
- **No priority-based rule here.** Priority → preference mapping is
  WL-0MVNUIW77000VYAX and layers on top of this default.
- **Interactive panes untouched.** No env var unless the operator exports
  `HERDR_LOCAL_PREFERENCE`; no new polling or logging behaviour.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/local-preference.ts`: `DOWNTIME_LOCAL_PREFERENCE =
  'local-only'`, `BACKGROUND_LOCAL_PREFERENCE = 'remote-ok'`;
  `clampDowntimeLocalPreference()` returns `DOWNTIME_LOCAL_PREFERENCE` for
  anything not in the two-value alphabet.
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts`: `defaultSettings.downtimeLocalPreference`
  uses the constant; `loadSettings()` clamps the persisted value through
  `clampDowntimeLocalPreference`, so absent/invalid already follows the
  constant (only the constant needs to change for AC1–AC3 to hold).
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` forwards `s.downtimeLocalPreference` into the
  worker config and `s.downtimeLocalPreference`/`BACKGROUND_LOCAL_PREFERENCE`
  into the headless dispatcher.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` threads `localPreference` through
  `runDispatchTick` → `dispatchDowntimeWork` / `dispatchClaimedTier` →
  `spawnAgentPane` → `buildDowntimePaneArgs` (`--local-preference`) and
  `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions` (`HERDR_LOCAL_PREFERENCE`); the scheduled-prompt
  path uses `opts.localPreference ?? BACKGROUND_LOCAL_PREFERENCE`.
- Tests currently pinning the old default: `packages/herdr/src/local-preference.test.ts`
  (`DOWNTIME_LOCAL_PREFERENCE === 'local-only'`) and `tests/herdr/settings.test.ts`
  (default and invalid-value clamp cases). Forwarding tests
  (`downtime-worker.reserve.test.ts`, `tests/herdr/send-to-pi.test.ts`,
  `coordination-dispatch.test.ts`, `downtime-worker.tiers.test.ts`) pass explicit
  values and should stay green.
- Documentation currently stating the default: `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`
  (Policy knob paragraph), `packages/herdr/README.md` (setting list and the
  per-turn local preference section), `packages/tui/extensions/README.md`
  (policy-knob cross-reference).

## Desired change

1. Flip `DOWNTIME_LOCAL_PREFERENCE` to `'remote-ok'` and rewrite the module
   header + clamp doc comments so `local-only` reads as the explicit opt-in.
2. Update the `settings.ts` property comment and default wiring prose.
3. Update/add tests: new default (module + settings), absent-key and
   invalid-value clamping, unchanged verbatim pass-through, dispatch-path
   inheritance with no setting present, and the extension route-log
   `remote-ok` case.
4. Update the three documentation surfaces so the prose matches the code,
   including the explicit-`local-only` scheduled-prompt inheritance.
5. Record the supersession of the pinned C4-AC1 default on
   WL-0MVLJTV03000KIQZ (comment) so the changed decision is auditable.

**Key Files:**

- `packages/herdr/src/local-preference.ts` — flip the default constant and
  rewrite the policy doc comments (default vs opt-in, supersession note).
- `packages/herdr/src/local-preference.test.ts` — pin `remote-ok` as the
  downtime default; keep clamp tests expressed relative to the constant.
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — update the `downtimeLocalPreference`
  property comment; default already derives from the constant.
- `tests/herdr/settings.test.ts` — new default expectation and invalid-value
  clamp expectations (`'auto'`, `42` → `remote-ok`).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — comment prose for the
  `localPreference` field and dispatch paths (default now `remote-ok`).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.tiers.test.ts`,
  `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.reserve.test.ts`,
  `packages/herdr/src/coordination-dispatch.test.ts` — dispatch-path
  inheritance coverage (scheduled prompt, own-backlog fallback, audit-batch
  continuation) with no setting present.
- `packages/tui/extensions/local-preference/local-preference.test.ts` —
  route-log line with `preference: 'remote-ok'` (and header injection already
  covered for both values).
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — Policy knob paragraph (default, opt-in,
  scheduled inheritance).
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — setting list entry and the per-turn local
  preference section.
- `packages/tui/extensions/README.md` — policy-knob prose if it implies a
  local-only default.

## Related work

- **WL-0MVLJTV03000KIQZ** (completed, *Per-turn local preference and route
  logging*) — introduced the knob, the wire contract and the `local-only`
  downtime default (C4-AC1) that this item supersedes; its default-pinning
  tests are updated here.
- **WL-0MVIKRFP0005JDL8** (completed) — parent downtime-dispatch epic whose
  AC4 slice C4 defined the locality policy.
- **WL-0MVNUIW77000VYAX** (*Dispatch low-priority work items with local-only
  preference*) — layers priority → preference on top of this default; its
  "explicit operator setting always overrides" rule stays intact.
- **WL-0MVNUJG04005QL7G** (*local-only requests over the local provider context
  limits are unprocessable*) — the context-ceiling limitation that makes a
  blanket `local-only` default unattractive; separate scope.
- **WL-0MVNUMI1B0021IGI** (open test-failure, `downtime-worker.pane-spawn.test.ts`)
  — unrelated failure in the same package; expect possible slot contention when
  running the herdr suites, not a dependency.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk — cost/route shift.** `remote-ok` lets contended downtime work leave the
  box for a remote (possibly metered) provider. That is the intended trade
  ("never queue local capacity"), but it is a real change in spend profile;
  `local-only` stays the one-line opt-in and the route log makes the route
  visible. Document it, do not hide it.
- **Risk — silently superseding a pinned AC.** C4-AC1 (WL-0MVLJTV03000KIQZ)
  explicitly pinned `local-only`. Mitigation: the brief records the
  supersession, the code comment names it, and a comment is added to the
  predecessor item.
- **Risk — implicit-default migration.** Deployments that never wrote
  `downtimeLocalPreference` start going remote on contention. Intended, but it
  must be called out in the docs (and the release note handled by `/skill:ship`).
- **Risk — hidden default assumptions in tests.** Only
  `local-preference.test.ts` and `tests/herdr/settings.test.ts` were found
  asserting the old default; the changed-scope gate should confirm nothing else
  depends on it.
- **Assumption.** No proxy/LP change is required: the wire alphabet and headers
  are unchanged, only which value herdr prefers by default.
- **Assumption.** No settings migration is written: an explicit
  `'local-only'` value keeps working verbatim; only absent/invalid input
  resolves to the new default.
- **Scope-creep guard.** Priority-aware preference, context-ceiling routing and
  any "auto" heuristic stay in WL-0MVNUIW77000VYAX / WL-0MVNUJG04005QL7G — not
  here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interactive questions were required — the seed context (goal, exact file,
AC list and related items) was sufficient to draft this brief. Decisions that
would otherwise have been questions were resolved from repo evidence:

- Q: "Does `clampDowntimeLocalPreference` need a separate change, or does it
  follow the constant?" — Answer (research): follows the constant — it returns
  `DOWNTIME_LOCAL_PREFERENCE` for anything not in the alphabet
  (`packages/herdr/src/local-preference.ts`), so the single constant flip makes
  absent/invalid resolve to `remote-ok`. Source: repo inspection. Recorded as
  AC2 to keep the fail-open behaviour explicit.
- Q: "Do scheduled prompts and headless background dispatches need their own
  change?" — Answer (research): no — both already resolve to
  `BACKGROUND_LOCAL_PREFERENCE` (`'remote-ok'`) when no knob is supplied
  (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` `dispatchScheduledPrompt`,
  `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` `spawnBackgroundPi`), and with the new default
  the knob itself is `remote-ok`. Explicit `local-only` deployments inherit the
  knob, which must be documented (Constraint). Source: repo inspection.
- Q: "Which tests and docs assert the old default?" — Answer (research):
  `packages/herdr/src/local-preference.test.ts` and
  `tests/herdr/settings.test.ts` assert it; `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`,
  `packages/herdr/README.md` and `packages/tui/extensions/README.md` describe
  it. Source: `grep` over the main checkout.
- Q: "Does changing the default contradict completed work?" — Answer
  (research): yes — WL-0MVLJTV03000KIQZ C4-AC1 pinned `local-only`. This item
  supersedes that default; the supersession is recorded here and on the
  predecessor item rather than left implicit. Source: `wl show
  WL-0MVLJTV03000KIQZ`.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MVNUIW77000VYAX** – Dispatch low-priority work items with local-only preference (open)
- **WL-0MSL2ZQIF006QB4Q** – Herdr isIdleStatus: prefer local_active_query over global active_query for idle detection (completed)
- **WL-0MT2GITCX009WUEW** – Remove packages/herdr/src/icons.ts and rewire herdr consumers (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: 0mvikrfp0005jdl8, 0mvljtv03000kiqz, absent, ac1, ac2 (+345 more)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: 0mvikrfp0005jdl8, 0mvljtv03000kiqz, absent, ac1, ac2 (+343 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: absent, ac2, add, added, already (+264 more)

# Dispatch low-priority work items with local-only preference

**Headline:** Let the dispatch layer derive a pane's locality preference from
the candidate's work-item priority — `low` → `local-only`, everything else →
the deployment default — while an operator who persisted
`downtimeLocalPreference` keeps that value for every dispatch, and record the
resolved preference plus its reason in the dispatch marker.

## Problem statement

Cheap, low-value work should absorb contention on the local slot instead of
competing for remote capacity, while `medium`/`high`/`critical` work keeps the
fail-fast remote route. Today locality is decided per pane from one
deployment-wide knob (`downtimeLocalPreference`, default `remote-ok` since
WL-0MVNUHWH500196K1), even though the candidate's priority is already resolved
at dispatch time and carried through the same plumbing
(`DowntimeCandidate.priority` → `mapDowntimeRequestPriority` →
`HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY`). Priority therefore has no influence on the locality
decision it could inform.

## Users

- **Producer/operator running downtime dispatch.** Wants low-priority backlog
  work to stay on the local slot (cheap work absorbs contention) while
  medium/high/critical work is never queued behind it locally.
- **Operator of an explicit locality policy.** Wants `downtimeLocalPreference:
  local-only` (or `remote-ok`) to keep meaning "every downtime pane", with no
  priority-dependent surprises.
- **Operator auditing dispatch behaviour.** Wants the dispatch marker to state
  which preference was used and why (`priority-low` rule vs deployment
  default vs operator setting), so the choice is evidence rather than
  guesswork.

User stories:

- As a producer, I want a `low`-priority item dispatched with
  `local-only` so cheap work uses the local slot and fails fast instead of
  consuming remote capacity.
- As a producer, I want a `high`-priority item dispatched with the deployment
  default (`remote-ok`) so urgent unattended work never stalls on a contended
  local slot.
- As an operator who set `downtimeLocalPreference` explicitly, I want that
  value applied to every downtime pane regardless of item priority.
- As an operator, I want each dispatch marker to record the resolved
  preference and its reason so I can confirm the rule fired.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Pure resolver.** `resolveDispatchLocalPreference(priority,
  defaultPreference)` is a pure, IO-free function in
  `packages/herdr/src/local-preference.ts` returning `'local-only'` for
  `priority === 'low'` and `defaultPreference` verbatim for every other input
  (`medium`, `high`, `critical`, `undefined`, `null`, `''`, unknown strings),
  unit-tested in `packages/herdr/src/local-preference.test.ts`.
- [ ] **Precedence.** The dispatch decision is: explicit operator setting
  (persisted, valid `downtimeLocalPreference`) **>** priority rule (**low** →
  `local-only`; everything else → `DOWNTIME_LOCAL_PREFERENCE`, currently
  `remote-ok`) **>** deployment default. Tests pin all three branches,
  including an explicit `remote-ok` deployment where a `low`-priority dispatch
  still forwards `remote-ok`.
- [ ] **Explicitness detection.** `loadSettings` exposes whether the operator
  persisted the knob (a derived, never-persisted signal: a valid
  `local-only`/`remote-ok` value present in the settings file); absent,
  missing-file and out-of-alphabet values all resolve to "not explicit" so the
  priority rule applies. `defaultSettings.downtimeLocalPreference` stays
  `'remote-ok'` and `clampDowntimeLocalPreference` keeps its two-value
  alphabet (WL-0MVNUHWH500196K1 ACs unchanged).
- [ ] **All dispatch paths.** The resolution happens once at the dispatch
  boundary (`dispatchClaimedTier`), so coordination-offer, own-backlog
  fallback, audit-batch continuation, critical-first/normal scan and the
  legacy tier chain all inherit it; scheduled-prompt dispatch (no work item,
  no priority) resolves to the deployment default and records that reason.
  Absent legacy flag/config keeps today's byte-identical forwarding for
  hand-built configs and existing tests.
- [ ] **Marker evidence.** The downtime dispatch marker
  (`.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`) records the resolved
  `localPreference` and a machine-readable `localPreferenceReason`
  (`priority-low` | `default` | `operator-setting`); scheduled-prompt markers
  record theirs too. Marker readers stay backward compatible (unknown/absent
  fields ignored).
- [ ] **Observable route.** Regression tests assert a `low`-priority dispatch
  spawns with `local-only` (`--local-preference local-only` /
  `HERDR_LOCAL_PREFERENCE=local-only`) and a `high`-priority dispatch with the
  deployment default, so the Worklog extension's route log shows the
  corresponding `preference` value.
- [ ] **Documentation.** `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` and
  `packages/herdr/README.md` state the precedence order (explicit setting >
  priority rule > default), the marker fields and the scheduled-prompt
  behaviour; `packages/tui/extensions/README.md`'s knob cross-reference gains
  the one-line precedence note; related code comments in `local-preference.ts`,
  `settings.ts`, `dispatch-claims.ts` and the worker contract are updated.
- [ ] **Testing/validation gate.** Changed-scope tests pass before commit and
  the full project test suite passes via `/skill:test` (no ad-hoc test runs).

## Constraints

- **Wire contract unchanged.** `X-Local-Preference` stays exactly
  `local-only | remote-ok`; no new header, value or proxy (LP) change is in
  scope. The priority rule chooses between the existing two values.
- **Two-value settings alphabet preserved.** `downtimeLocalPreference` keeps
  accepting `local-only | remote-ok` only; explicitness is a *derived*
  property, not a new persisted token (rejected alternative: an `auto` token,
  which would supersede WL-0MVNUHWH500196K1's pinned default/clamp ACs while it
  is still in review).
- **Legacy callers unchanged.** A hand-built `DowntimeWorkerConfig` /
  `dispatchClaimedTier` caller that supplies `localPreference` without the new
  opt-in flag keeps forwarding that value verbatim (byte-identical launch, no
  marker fields added). Only the plugin's `config()` opts a deployment into the
  priority rule, and only when the setting was not persisted.
- **Fail-open preserved.** Resolution never throws and never invents a value:
  unknown priority → deployment default; unknown/absent setting → the
  documented clamp result. The priority lookup is not repeated — the already
  resolved `DowntimeCandidate.priority` is used.
- **Reservation handshake untouched.** `buildLocalReservationRequest` keeps
  `priority: 'background'`; a `local-only` pane still asks for a local ticket
  (the rule changes the per-turn preference, not the admission protocol).
- **Scheduled prompt inheritance unchanged.** Scheduled prompts continue to
  inherit the knob when present and fall back to `BACKGROUND_LOCAL_PREFERENCE`
  (also `remote-ok`) when the config supplies nothing.
- **Gate-gap awareness.** `tests/herdr/**` and
  `packages/tui/extensions/**/*.test.ts` are outside the configured
  `suiteCommands` (WL-0MVG4FF9200346NR), so new coverage must live in
  `packages/herdr/src/*.test.ts` to be executed by the `herdr` group; any
  `tests/herdr` edit is documented as such.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/local-preference.ts` — `LocalPreference`,
  `LOCAL_PREFERENCE_ENV_VAR`, `DOWNTIME_LOCAL_PREFERENCE = 'remote-ok'`,
  `BACKGROUND_LOCAL_PREFERENCE = 'remote-ok'`,
  `clampDowntimeLocalPreference()`. No priority-aware helper exists.
- `packages/herdr/src/request-priority.ts` — `mapDowntimeRequestPriority()`
  already maps work-item priority → `X-Priority` (`low` stays `low`,
  `critical` → `high`, unknown → `medium`); priority is therefore available
  and already threaded to the pane, but the locality decision ignores it.
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — `PluginSettings.downtimeLocalPreference:
  LocalPreference`; `defaultSettings` uses the constant; `loadSettings`
  clamps the persisted value. There is no signal distinguishing "operator
  persisted the key" from "clamped default".
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `config()` passes
  `localPreference: s.downtimeLocalPreference` into the worker config;
  `spawnBackgroundPi` falls back to `BACKGROUND_LOCAL_PREFERENCE`.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.orchestrator-dispatch.ts` — forwards
  `cfg.localPreference` into both `dispatchFromCoordination` and
  `dispatchDowntimeWork`.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts` — offer path,
  `dispatchFromOwnHead` (own-backlog fallback + audit-batch continuation) and
  the scheduled-prompt stage all forward `opts.localPreference`.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-filter.ts` /
  `downtime-worker.dispatch.ts` — critical-first / normal scan contexts
  forward `ctx.localPreference` into `dispatchClaimedTier`.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-claims.ts` —
  `dispatchClaimedTier` holds the candidate (`priority` available), writes the
  success marker (`recordDispatch`), and forwards `opts.localPreference` to
  `spawnAgentPane`; `dispatchScheduledPrompt` writes its own marker and spawns
  with `opts.localPreference ?? BACKGROUND_LOCAL_PREFERENCE`.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-contract.ts` —
  `DowntimeDispatchEvent` carries `itemId`/`kind`/`dispatchedAt`/`stage`/
  `selectionPath`/`selectionReason`/`reservationTicketId` (+`GrantedAt`).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts` — `DowntimeLogEntry` and the
  marker readers (`dispatchedItemMarkers`, `markerStillExcludes`) ignore
  unknown fields, so new marker fields are backward compatible.
- `packages/tui/extensions/local-preference/` — reads
  `HERDR_LOCAL_PREFERENCE` per request, sets `X-Local-Preference`, writes the
  route log (`preference` field); needs no behavioural change, only its tests
  are the reference for the expected route-log observation.
- Tests already pinning forwarding: `packages/herdr/src/local-preference.test.ts`
  (defaults/clamp), `downtime-worker.reserve.test.ts` (pane args/env + dispatch
  → spawn thread), `downtime-worker.tiers.test.ts` / `coordination-dispatch.test.ts`
  (scheduled prompt, offer, fallback, continuation forwarding with explicit
  values) and `tests/herdr/settings.test.ts` (setting default/clamp).

## Desired change

1. Add the pure resolver plus a small reason type to
   `local-preference.ts`, with the module header documenting the precedence
   order and cross-referencing WL-0MVNUHWH500196K1 (default) and this item
   (priority rule).
2. Add the derived explicitness signal to `settings.ts` (`PluginSettings` +
   `defaultSettings` + `loadSettings`), documented as derived and
   never-persisted, and keep the persisted alphabet and default unchanged.
3. Plumb the "apply priority rule" opt-in beside `localPreference` through
   `index.ts config()` → worker config → orchestrator → coordination leader /
   dispatch filter → `dispatchClaimedTier` (absent = fixed legacy behaviour).
4. Resolve the preference once in `dispatchClaimedTier` from
   `candidate.priority`, record `localPreference` + `localPreferenceReason` on
   the success marker, and forward the resolved value to `spawnAgentPane`;
   mirror the marker fields for `dispatchScheduledPrompt` (deployment default,
   no priority).
5. Extend `DowntimeDispatchEvent` and `DowntimeLogEntry` with the two optional
   marker fields; keep readers and legacy entries unchanged.
6. Tests: resolver table, precedence branches (explicit `local-only` /
   explicit `remote-ok` with a low-priority candidate / no setting), settings
   explicitness derivation, marker fields for all paths, scheduled-prompt
   marker, and pane forwarding for a low vs high candidate.
7. Documentation: precedence order, marker fields and scheduled-prompt
   behaviour in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` and
   `packages/herdr/README.md`; one-line precedence note in
   `packages/tui/extensions/README.md`; code comments updated.

**Key Files:**

- `packages/herdr/src/local-preference.ts` — add
  `resolveDispatchLocalPreference(priority, defaultPreference)` + the reason
  vocabulary; document the precedence order.
- `packages/herdr/src/local-preference.test.ts` — resolver table (low,
  medium/high/critical, absent/unknown, default passed through verbatim).
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — derived `downtimeLocalPreferenceExplicit`
  in `PluginSettings`/`defaultSettings`/`loadSettings`; property comment.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `config()` forwards the explicitness opt-in
  beside `localPreference` to the worker.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.worker-contract.ts` — worker config and
  `spawnAgentPane` docs gain the opt-in flag.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-contract.ts` —
  `dispatchClaimedTier` opts flag + `localPreference` /
  `localPreferenceReason` on `DowntimeDispatchEvent`.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-claims.ts` — resolve once,
  record marker fields, forward the resolved value; scheduled-prompt
  resolution.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.orchestrator-dispatch.ts`,
  `downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts`,
  `downtime-worker.dispatch-filter.ts`, `downtime-worker.dispatch.ts` —
  thread the opt-in flag through the existing `localPreference` plumbing.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts` — `DowntimeLogEntry` gains the two
  optional marker fields + docs.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.reserve.test.ts` — dispatch → spawn
  forwarding for low vs medium/high; explicit-setting override.
- `packages/herdr/src/coordination-dispatch.test.ts` — offer, own-backlog
  fallback and audit-batch continuation resolve from priority.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.tiers.test.ts` — legacy tier chain and
  scheduled-prompt marker/preference.
- `tests/herdr/settings.test.ts` — explicitness derivation cases (outside the
  configured suite commands — see Constraints; mirror any critical case in
  `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.settings.test.ts`).
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — precedence order, marker fields, route
  log expectation.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — setting description + per-turn section
  precedence.
- `packages/tui/extensions/README.md` — one-line precedence cross-reference.

## Related work

- **WL-0MVNUHWH500196K1** (completed, *Default downtime local preference should
  be remote-ok*) — flipped `DOWNTIME_LOCAL_PREFERENCE` to `remote-ok` and
  explicitly excluded the priority rule ("No priority-based rule here …
  layers on top of this default"). This item implements that layer and leaves
  its default/clamp/settings ACs intact.
- **WL-0MVLJTV03000KIQZ** (completed, *Per-turn local preference and route
  logging*) — introduced the knob, the `X-Local-Preference` wire contract and
  the route log this item's observable evidence relies on.
- **WL-0MVIKRFP0005JDL8** (completed, *Herdr downtime dispatch: claim local
  capacity via proxy reservation*) — parent epic whose AC4/slice C4 defined the
  locality policy.
- **WL-0MVF3Q3VL000UNCN** (completed, *Interactive dispatch request priority*)
  — supplied `DowntimeCandidate.priority` → `X-Priority`, the input this rule
  consumes.
- **WL-0MVNUJG04005QL7G** (open, *local-only requests over the local provider
  context limits are unprocessable*) — a `local-only` pane whose prompt exceeds
  the local context ceiling fails; a low-priority item with a large prompt can
  now hit it. Separate scope, watch for interaction.
- **WL-0MVG4FF9200346NR** (open, plan complete, *Canonical test suite excludes
  77 root-level tests/test.ts files*) — the gate gap that leaves
  `tests/herdr/**` unexecuted; drives the test placement constraint.
- **WL-0MVNUMI1B0021IGI** (completed, test-failure) — pre-existing
  `downtime-worker.pane-spawn.test.ts` failure in the same package; expect slot
  contention when running the herdr group, not a dependency.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk — cheap work now fails fast locally.** A `low`-priority pane on a
  contended local slot is refused immediately (by design) instead of waiting
  or going remote, so low-priority backlog can stall while the operator holds
  the slot. That is the intended trade ("absorb contention locally"), and the
  explicit-setting override plus the route log keep it controllable and
  visible.
- **Risk — new derived settings field leaks into `saveSettings`.** The
  explicitness signal must stay derived; persisting it would make every
  explicit deployment permanently explicit after one save. Mitigation: it is
  documented as derived, `saveSettings`/documented JSON omit it, and a test
  writes settings and re-reads the derived value from the presence of the
  persisted knob only.
- **Risk — plumbing churn.** The opt-in flag crosses ~8 files; a missed path
  silently keeps the fixed behaviour. Mitigation: resolve only inside
  `dispatchClaimedTier` (single decision point), and assert each named dispatch
  path (offer / fallback / continuation / scheduled / legacy chain) in tests.
- **Risk — marker/reader compatibility.** New fields must be ignored by
  existing readers; `markerStillExcludes` and `dispatchedItemMarkers` already
  ignore unknown fields, and legacy entries simply omit them.
- **Risk — explicit-`remote-ok` surprise.** Deployments that wrote
  `downtimeLocalPreference: 'remote-ok'` explicitly will *not* get the
  low-priority rule (their setting wins). Documented as the precedence order;
  `wl comment` on WL-0MVNUHWH500196K1 is not needed, but the docs must say how
  to opt into the rule (remove the key).
- **Assumption.** Priority comes from the already resolved
  `DowntimeCandidate.priority`; no extra `wl show` lookup is added (no new IO,
  no new timeout).
- **Assumption.** The rule applies uniformly to every downtime kind (audit,
  implement, plan, intake, risk-effort) — it keys on the candidate's priority
  only; a low-priority audit is still low-priority work.
- **Assumption.** Scheduled prompts have no work item and therefore no
  priority; they resolve to the deployment default and record
  `localPreferenceReason: 'default'` (or `operator-setting`).
- **Scope-creep guard.** Context-ceiling handling (WL-0MVNUJG04005QL7G),
  reservation-request priority, a new `auto` settings token, a settings UI and
  any per-kind exemptions stay out of scope — record them as new items if they
  become necessary.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interactive questions were required — the seed context (goal, proposed
rule, exact ACs and the cross-referenced default-flip item) was sufficient to
draft this brief. Decisions that would otherwise have been questions were
resolved from repo evidence:

- Q: "How can the dispatch layer tell an explicit operator setting from the
  deployment default, when `loadSettings` always returns a clamped value?" —
  Answer (research/design): add a **derived, never-persisted** explicitness
  signal computed in `loadSettings` (true only when the settings file contains
  a valid `local-only`/`remote-ok`), keep the two-value persisted alphabet and
  the `remote-ok` default, and thread a single "apply priority rule" opt-in
  that only the plugin's `config()` sets (when the key is absent). Source:
  `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` (`loadSettings` merge/clamp),
  WL-0MVNUHWH500196K1 Constraints ("config() always supplies a value"). The
  rejected alternative — an `auto` settings token — would supersede that
  item's pinned default/clamp ACs while it is still in review.
- Q: "Does the priority rule apply to audit dispatches too?" — Answer
  (research/AC text): yes — the AC keys on "the candidate's priority is low",
  with no kind exemption; audit/implement/plan/intake/risk-effort share the
  same `DowntimeCandidate.priority`. Source: this item's ACs;
  `dispatchClaimedTier` receives the candidate for every kind.
- Q: "What about scheduled prompts, which have no work item?" — Answer
  (research): no priority exists, so they resolve to the deployment default
  (`BACKGROUND_LOCAL_PREFERENCE`/knob, both `remote-ok` today) and record
  `localPreferenceReason: 'default'`; an explicit operator setting still wins
  through the same precedence. Source:
  `dispatchScheduledPrompt` in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-claims.ts`.
- Q: "Where should resolution happen so all four named paths agree?" — Answer
  (research): at the single dispatch boundary `dispatchClaimedTier`, which
  every path (coordination offer, own-backlog fallback, audit-batch
  continuation, legacy tier chain) funnels through with the candidate in hand.
  Source: `dispatchClaimedTier` call sites in
  `downtime-worker.dispatch-filter.ts`,
  `downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts`, `downtime-worker.dispatch.ts`.
- Q: "Do existing forwarding tests break?" — Answer (research): no — they pass
  a concrete `localPreference` without the new opt-in, which stays
  "fixed/explicit" behaviour; only the plugin path (absent persisted key) opts
  into the rule. Source: `localPreference` usages in
  `downtime-worker.tiers.test.ts`, `downtime-worker.reserve.test.ts`,
  `coordination-dispatch.test.ts`.
- Q: "Should the marker's reason vocabulary include the operator-setting
  case, or only 'priority rule vs default'?" — Answer (design): include it —
  the seed AC asks for the reason so the choice is auditable, and without an
  `operator-setting` value an explicit `remote-ok` deployment would record
  `default`, hiding the fact that the priority rule was bypassed. Source: this
  item's AC text plus the precedence rule in AC2.
- Duplicate check: `wl search` ("priority preference local-only low-priority")
  surfaced only this item and WL-0MVNUHWH500196K1, whose brief explicitly
  excludes the priority rule — no overlapping/duplicate item, so this item is
  the distinct implementation of the layered rule.

data.description:
Goal: a local-only pane whose prompt exceeds the local provider's context ceiling should degrade predictably instead of stalling or failing, and the reason should be visible to the operator.

Observed problem: the local provider rejects a local-only request when the projected prompt exceeds ~38k tokens warm, or ~25k on a cold prefix. Because the pane is labelled local-only the proxy refuses the local route, and the work is not processed on the local slot. Evidence in this deployment's route logs (.worklog/local-route.log, 697 turns across 5 roots): 49 turns route remote with fallbackReason resident_prefix_insufficient and 44 with large_context_bypass; 72 turns actually served local. The thresholds and the exact refusal behaviour (hard error vs silent fallback) live in the external llama-proxy (LP project), not in this repo - confirm before designing the fix.

Open design questions to settle in plan:
- Is the correct behaviour a fallback to remote for over-threshold requests, an explicit hard error surfaced to the operator, or pre-dispatch routing (choose remote-ok when the projected context exceeds the ceiling)?
- Where is the projected context size knowable? The pi extension sees the outgoing request (before_provider_headers), the dispatcher does not.
- Interaction with WL-0MVNUIW77000VYAX (low priority -> local-only): over-threshold low-priority work must not become unprocessable.

ACs:
- [ ] Reproduce the failure deterministically (unit test or scripted proxy stub) for a prompt above 38k warm and above 25k cold, recording the observed proxy response headers.
- [ ] Document the confirmed thresholds and the refusal semantics (hard error vs fallback) in docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md.
- [ ] A local-only request over the ceiling produces a deterministic, observable outcome - no silent stall - with the reason recorded in .worklog/local-route.log.
- [ ] The chosen mitigation (fallback, hard error, or pre-dispatch routing) is covered by tests on both sides of each threshold.
- [ ] Operators can see over-threshold refusals without reading raw JSONL (documented query/ or herdr view).
- [ ] Full test suite green.

# tree_coverage AC extraction silently ignores numbered acceptance-criteria lists

discovered-from:WL-0MVGB23MM004X501

## Problem

`skill/shared/tree_coverage.py` (`extract_acceptance_criteria`) only collects
markdown bullets that start with `- ` or `+ ` inside the `## Acceptance Criteria`
section. Work items whose ACs are a **numbered** list (`1. …`, `2. …`) yield an
empty AC set, so `run_coverage_review` reports `fully_covered: true` /
`recommendation: proceed` with **zero parent ACs** — the AC coverage gate passes
vacuously instead of verifying that children cover the parent.

Observed during planning of WL-0MVGB23MM004X501: `apply_coverage_review` returned
`action: proceed` with `parent_acs: 0` against a description containing nine
numbered ACs. Contributors have worked around it by manually normalising AC lists
to `- ` bullets (e.g. WL-0MVGYLU0S004WZUS, WL-0MV02VA29009WBEN) or by documenting
the limitation (WL-0MUVSQ4EO00092E7), which means the failure mode is invisible
unless an operator notices a 0-AC result.

## Desired outcome

1. `extract_acceptance_criteria` also parses numbered list items (`1. `, `1) `)
   inside the AC section, keeping continuation lines and inline code intact.
2. A parent section that has a `## Acceptance Criteria` heading but yields zero
   parsed ACs is reported as a **conflict/stop condition** (or an explicit
   warning in the review result) rather than silently `proceed`, so a silent
   vacuous pass is impossible.
3. Existing bullet-form ACs and all currently passing coverage reviews are
   unaffected (regression tests over both formats).
4. Documentation in the plan/intake skills notes the supported AC formats.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Numbered AC lists (`1. …`) and bullet lists (`- …`) are both extracted by
  `extract_acceptance_criteria`, with matching output for equivalent content.
- A numbered AC list in a work item description produces a non-zero
  `parent_acs` count from `run_coverage_review`.
- An `## Acceptance Criteria` section that parses to zero ACs no longer returns
  `recommendation: proceed` silently — it is surfaced as a conflict or explicit
  warning in the review result.
- Unit tests cover: numbered list, bullet list, mixed list, empty AC section, and
  the zero-AC stop/warn behaviour.
- Plan and intake skill docs state which AC formats the tooling recognises.

## Notes

- Workaround for items already affected: normalise the AC list to `- ` bullets
  (wording unchanged) so coverage can be computed.
data.title: tree_coverage AC extraction ignores numbered acceptance-criteria lists
